profile.reading: K-Motion Interactive is a sports-technology company that makes 3D motion-capture and biomechanics analysis systems used in golf and baseball swing instruction, based in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona. The coordinates on file sit within the McDowell Mountain Business Park, a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park, and a check of the address today finds a different small business occupying that specific building. There is no indication that K-Motion, or any current tenant at this location, operates server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated data center infrastructure here. This entry describes the business as it is known publicly rather than presenting an ordinary office address as a data center facility.

reading.body:
K-Motion Interactive is not a data center, and its listing as one is an artifact of a mistagged OpenStreetMap point. The company makes 3D motion-capture and biomechanics analysis systems for golf and baseball instruction. The coordinates on file resolve to a different small business in a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park in Scottsdale, Arizona. No server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated data center infrastructure are present at that address.

The mistag is not a single stray record. The other eight rows in the same batch sit 12 to 15 miles away, across Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, and Gilbert, so they are not one shared building either. The common factor is that each is an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro. Inventories assembled from volunteered map data inherit that error at the level of the count, before any question of capacity is even asked.

For AI scaling the count is the weaker number and published power is the stronger one. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, and only 4 of them publish power figures, totaling 512 MW. A mistagged office contributes nothing to that 512 MW and no compute to the grid. The error inflates the apparent density of Arizona data center sites while leaving the only figure that bears on AI scaling untouched.

What this does not establish is how many other entries in the Arizona inventory are mistagged, or whether the 52 facilities without published power figures are real data centers with undisclosed load or further errors of the same kind. It also says nothing about K-Motion's business beyond its public description. The entry should be removed from any inventory of data center capacity in Arizona.
